ratings.rationale: Association tampering is valid central L3 software threat; no published mechanism. It can create, merge or lose tracks, giving deception, denial or displacement. Ground/insider access T2; P evidence lowers reproducibility.
ratings.issue: No published mechanism; three outcomes make damage ambiguous.

ratings.rationale: Altering integrity logic can mask bias or false-flag tracks; central check compromise makes detection unlikely. No cited mechanism, so P. Ground/insider T2; damage scored as possible displacement.
ratings.issue: Includes monitor and cross-check; could be split; no cited mechanism.

ratings.rationale: Corrupt ephemeris/clock-state store is valid tampering that injects timing-like bias into solver; if unflagged it displaces targets. P evidence; insider/ground T2. Strong-pass checks may catch, weak-pass stealth.
ratings.issue: Assets include solver although attack is on database; overlaps timing-bias threats.

ratings.rationale: Post-association observable tampering is distinct data-integrity threat inside solver; can bias positions. No published mechanism. Process access implies T2. Detection possible at L3 in strong pass but weak-pass stealth.
ratings.issue: Overlaps T3.03 as solver-input tampering; process access boundary unclear.

ratings.rationale: Resource exhaustion of solver/tracker has denial consequence; plausible via message flooding. Cited talk is not peer-reviewed/unknown, so conservative E1. T1c RF emitter; central effect regional.
ratings.issue: Source #65 not peer-reviewed and unassessed; DoS may be enabler.

ratings.rationale: Raising integrity thresholds does not itself alter a report; it widens stealth window, so enabler. No mechanism cited. Overlaps logic tampering; configuration access T2.
ratings.issue: Likely enabler; authors may overstate direct damage; overlaps T3.02.

ratings.rationale: Synchronised emitters corrupt both independent positions, bypassing cross-check and yielding verified false track. Peer-reviewed but analogue terrestrial evidence; T2. No L3 check catches consistent spoof.
ratings.issue: Layer/asset scoping weak: physical emitters are L1/TB0; evidence analogue.

ratings.rationale: Perturbing one position of an honest aircraft creates false discrepancy and discredits it; deception not displacement. Evidence analogue; local RF emitter T1c. Cross-check detects discrepancy at L3 but misattributes.
ratings.issue: Perturbing one position is closer to spoofing than L3 tampering; evidence analogue.

ratings.rationale: Encoder/gateway tampering sits downstream of detection and can alter position or integrity annotation. No cited mechanism; ground/insider T2. Platform compromise may subsume it.
ratings.issue: No cited mechanism; overlaps platform compromise T3.12.

ratings.rationale: Disclosure of tracks is a valid information threat with disclosure-only damage; not enabler. Asset scoping is poor: track stores/logs extend beyond A3.6. No published mechanism.
ratings.issue: Asset mis-scoped: track database/logs are A3.3/A3.7/A4.5, not only A3.6.

ratings.rationale: Log suppression only impedes attribution; no direct target-report consequence, so enabler. Asset likely platform/log store rather than A3.3. Cited talk unknown; conservative E1.
ratings.issue: Enabler only; log store likely A3.7/A4.8 rather than A3.3.

ratings.rationale: CPS platform compromise gives control of all L3 modules; broad but valid. Cited talk unknown, conservative E1. T2 ground/insider; no L3 check survives, whole-constellation impact.
ratings.issue: Broad threat subsumes T3.01-T3.09; source unassessed.

missing_threats.title: Ephemeris poisoning via orbit-determination feed
missing_threats.why: T3.03 covers direct store write but not compromised L4 ephemeris product supply.

missing_threats.title: PTP and synchronisation policy manipulation
missing_threats.why: Governance can bias clock/time transfer, bypassing L3 module tampering.

missing_threats.title: Telecommand or ground-station compromise
missing_threats.why: Commands and updates to payload/platform are a path to L1/L2 control absent here.

missing_threats.title: ATM feed injection or replay
missing_threats.why: Output tampering beyond ASTERIX encoder, at delivery/ATM interface, not covered.

missing_threats.title: ADS-B spoofing of honest aircraft
missing_threats.why: T3.08 assumes perturbation but no dedicated air-interface spoofing record.

rubric_ambiguities: Di_strong/Di_weak are defined via clock-bias STRONG/WEAK passes but applied to software/data threats where W2/W3 do not apply.
Enabler versus direct threat for threshold relaxation: no target-report consequence alone, but intent is to enable displacement.
Trust-boundary field unclear when asset register says none but attack requires platform/process access.
Evidence level for non-peer-reviewed attack-evidence talks; unknown sources force conservative P/E1.
Damage score when a threat lists multiple goals; rubric says consequence class but not max versus primary.
batch_comments.overall: Batch is mostly plausible L3 software/data-integrity threats, but evidence is weak and several records are broad or overlapping. T3.06 and T3.11 are enablers; T3.12 subsumes module-level tampering. Asset scoping and layer/trust-boundary assignments need tightening.
